title: Nobody saw this.
paragraphs:
No crowd.
No applause.
No miracles.
Just Jesus… alone in the dark.

Because the greatest power move in history…
happened where nobody was watching.
But here’s the tension we don’t talk about:

We want public power…
without private surrender.

We want God to use us…
but we avoid the place where He meets us.

We post.
We perform.
We serve.
We show up in church.

Silence feels uncomfortable.
Stillness feels threatening.
And suddenly… we reach for anything but God.
Because deep down, we’re afraid of what might surface when it’s just us and Him.
That’s where the real battle is.

You can look strong outside…
and still be starving inside.

You can speak about God…
and still feel distant from Him.

You can even serve in ministry…
and secretly avoid His presence.
Some of us are not running from sin…

It reveals the pride.
The hidden cravings.
The quiet compromises.
The wounds we buried but never healed.
And that’s exactly why Jesus went there.
“But Jesus often withdrew to lonely places and prayed.” — Luke 5:16

That means this wasn’t accidental.
This was intentional.
The Son of God—perfect, holy, sinless—still chose the lonely place.
Some scholars interpret this as Jesus modeling spiritual discipline. Others see it as a revelation of His deep, ongoing communion with the Father.
Either way, one thing is clear:

If Jesus needed the secret place…
we are foolish to think we don’t.
And this is where it gets personal.

Because the reason many of us avoid prayer…
is not lack of time.
We don’t want to sit still long enough to face what’s inside.
We’re afraid God will be disappointed.
The secret place is not where God exposes you to destroy you.
It’s where He meets you to restore you.
“Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts!” — Psalm 139:23
Because he knew something we forget:
And yet… He still invites you close.
This is where the Gospel explodes with beauty.
Because Jesus didn’t just pray alone in the night…
He also walked alone to the cross.
And on that cross, He carried everything you’re trying to hide.

Your sin.
Your shame.
Your inconsistency.
Your prayerlessness.
Your distractions.
Your secret battles.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not when you finally got your prayer life together.
And through His resurrection, He didn’t just forgive you—
He made a way for you to come back.
“Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace…” — Hebrews 4:16
You don’t enter God’s presence because you performed well.
You enter because Jesus paid fully.
So the question is no longer:

Because right now…
God is not waiting to reject you.
In the place you keep avoiding.
A quiet invitation from a loud, loving God.
And watch what happens when you stop running…
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
